To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the four-point scattering amplitudes in ABJM theory can be evaluated in terms of the same set of scalar Feyman integrals that are needed for the computation of Wilson loops.
we have computed the two-loop four-point scattering amplitude in ABJ theory, and we have compared it with a Wilson loop computed in a lightlike contour.

we have derived the set of scalar four-point Feynman integrands of ABJM theory in the = 2 formulation; we have computed the on-shell integrands using dimensional regularization and found matching results between Feynman and Wilson loop calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the computation of scattering amplitudes in the ABJM model.
the perturbative formulation and computation of scattering amplitudes in the ABJM theory.
the computation of the four-point amplitude in ABJM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two-loop ABJM four-point amplitude is not known in the literature and it is not known how to compute it.
, at the present time, the perturbative formulation in superspace for the ABJM theory is a very promising tool to study its perturbative aspects.

, in spite of the fact that the two-loop four-point scattering amplitude in ABJ(M) theory is still unknown, we have been able to provide an explicit expression for the corresponding Wilson-loop, which, in turn, has allowed us to compute the on-shell scalar integrals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have computed a set of Feynman integrands describing the four-point on-shell scattering of chiral fields in ABJM theory at two loops.

, within the = 2 ABJM superspace perturbatively formulation, we have derived and evaluated on-shell the set of scalar four-point Feynman integrand in ABJM theory and we have found a perfect matching of our result with the Wilson-loop computation in a light-like contour.
we have computed the four-point scattering amplitudes for the chiral matter fields in ABJM theory, and we have shown that it agrees with the Wilson loop calculation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the on-shell four-point amplitude of the ABJM theory can be obtained by evaluating a light-like Wilson-loop in the fundamental representation of SU(4) and with the coupling constant g = 4π.
, within the ABJM theory, the four‐point scattering amplitude of chilral matter fields and a light‐like Wilson loop are equivalent.
the four-point scattering in the ABJM theory can be computed using the Wilson-loop technique.
